title: hyper-markdown
excerpt: A strict, machine-checkable markdown dialect for project knowledge bases.
content_html:
Hyper-markdown (.hmd) is ordinary Markdown plus rich visuals plus wiki links into a knowledge graph. Every .md file is already valid .hmd.

Want to see it in action?

The HMD Tutorial is the whole language in one sitting — every construct, with its source shown beside what it renders.

TL;DR¶

  • A superset of CommonMark. Rename a .md file to .hmd and it is already valid — nothing breaks, and the format is adopted one file at a time.

  • Names, not paths. [[tokens]] is looked up beside the card and then upward through its parent folders. A name that could mean two documents is an error rather than a guess.

  • Documents made of documents. ![[glossary/token#^definition]] splices one named block into another page. Write a definition once and embed it everywhere it is needed.

  • Rich content is assumed, not optional. TeX mathematics, D2 diagrams, callouts, footnotes, task lists, and tables are part of what a card may carry. A diagram is text in the file and a diff you can read, and it degrades to its own labelled source rather than to a blank space.

  • The specification is the artifact. The Python CLI, the MkDocs plugin, and the VS Code extension are implementations around it; they conform to it rather than define it.

  • Version 0.x is a stage, not the scope. The resolver, linter, embed expander, renderer, and MkDocs plugin work today. Queries over the document graph and namespaces beyond one tree are specified in outline and unbuilt.

Language¶

Three layers stack in one file. At the base, CommonMark, inherited whole — nothing redefined and nothing taken away, which is why a .md file is already a valid card. Above it a rich layer — tables, footnotes, task lists, callouts, TeX mathematics, D2 diagrams — taken from the wider Markdown ecosystem rather than invented here, and assumed present rather than optional. And the hyper layer — arguably the most innovative part, and the reason the format exists at all: a small set of constructs that are all variations on one idea, naming another document or a part of one. Those upper two layers are what hyper-markdown adds, and a specification is what fixes them, not convention.

See [[tokens]] for the format, or pull one block in whole:

![[glossary/token#^definition]]

A card may open with YAML frontmatter, where four keys mean something to the toolchain — tags, use, import, nav — and every other key belongs to the author. The whole language fits on one page and can be learned in one sitting: the HMD Tutorial. What that page teaches, the HMD Language Specification states normatively.

Features¶

Wiki links to documents, headings, and named blocks; transclusion of any of them; filesystem-shaped modules with explicit imports; TeX mathematics, D2 diagrams, callouts, collapsible sections, footnotes, tables, and the GitHub- flavoured Markdown baseline. HQL, a query language over the document graph, is reserved and not yet designed.

What a page can carry, shown working rather than described, is Features. How a bare name becomes a page — the spine walk, imports, ambiguity as an error, and the module/namespace distinction — is Namespaces.

Tools¶

hmd lints a tree, renders a card to markdown or HTML, and dumps the resolved graph. A missing target is a warning, because writing forward is how a wiki grows; an ambiguous or malformed one is an error, because that is the one thing the format refuses to guess at.

There are three of them, one directory each under tools/ in the repository, each carrying its own version, README, and changelog:

  • hmd — the Python line, published to PyPI as hyper-markdown: the CLI (lint, render, graph), the library beneath it, and the MkDocs plugin that builds this site. Canonical — where two implementations disagree, this one defines the answer — and it will host the language server.

  • hmd-ts-core — @hyper-markdown/core, a second implementation of the format in TypeScript rather than extension code, answering to the same conformance corpus the canonical tool does.

  • hmd-vsc-ext — the VS Code extension, in development: live preview that keeps the embed boundary visible, plus backlinks, red links, and diagnostics.

Presentation is not part of the language. A card is plain text, so an editor, GitHub, or a chat window already shows it. The MkDocs plugin builds a tree of cards into a published site — this one, a hand-ordered book with a generated wiki inside it — and the extension renders one in the editor as it is typed. The trade-offs between them are Presentation.

The VS Code extension: the card's source on the left, the rendered card on the right, updated as it is typed.

Specification¶

The normative text is one document, the HMD Language Specification: what a card is, what each construct means, and what an implementation must do with it. It describes no particular program, and no program's behaviour overrides it.

It is stated against a named baseline — CommonMark 0.31.2 — because "markdown" names a family rather than a standard, and a superset of an unnamed dialect specifies nothing. And it is versioned apart from the tools that implement it: a release of hmd does not imply a new language version, and a language version does not wait for one. Where two implementations disagree about something the text leaves under-determined, the language-neutral conformance corpus decides.

The language is at 0.1. The text is drafted, and it will move before 1.0.

How it gets there is a separate process, and deliberately a formal one. A change is argued out first as a numbered technical proposal — HMD-0001, HMD-0002, and so on — in the style of RFCs and lightweight ADRs: a problem, the decision taken, the alternatives rejected, and a tracker of its own. Most of them are not about the language at all, and cover the tools and the presentation layer instead: how a bare name is resolved on disk, what the linter reports, how a tree of cards becomes a published site. They are working documents, kept for their motivation and their rejected alternatives, and where one disagrees with the specification the specification is right. The index is Proposals.

Vision¶

Markdown became the default plain text, and never got the part HTML had on its first day — links that mean something because they point into a knowledge graph, and a page that is part of a web rather than a file in a folder. Almost none of the ideas here are new; what is being attempted is a coherent specification of them.

The longer argument is that this should not stop at one repository: independently authored and independently served hyper-markdown, named across the gap, read from the same source by humans, tools, and AI. That argument, and how much of it is still unbuilt, is Vision.

Status¶

Pre-release. The scanner, resolver, linter, embed expander, renderer, and MkDocs plugin are implemented and tested. The language specification is at 0.1 and will still move. The living example is the wiki, generated from .hmd cards in this repository; the exhaustive inventory of every feature, where the idea came from, and what is deferred or turned down is the feature list.

blocks.html_en: Specification¶

sentences.en: Specification¶

blocks.html_en: The normative text is one document, the HMD Language Specification: what a card is, what each construct means, and what an implementation must do with it. It describes no particular program, and no program's behaviour overrides it.

sentences.en: It describes no particular program, and no program's behaviour overrides it.
sentences.zh: 它没有描述任何特定的程序，也没有程序的行为会覆盖它。

blocks.html_en: It is stated against a named baseline — CommonMark 0.31.2 — because "markdown" names a family rather than a standard, and a superset of an unnamed dialect specifies nothing. And it is versioned apart from the tools that implement it: a release of hmd does not imply a new language version, and a language version does not wait for one. Where two implementations disagree about something the text leaves under-determined, the language-neutral conformance corpus decides.

blocks.html_en: How it gets there is a separate process, and deliberately a formal one. A change is argued out first as a numbered technical proposal — HMD-0001, HMD-0002, and so on — in the style of RFCs and lightweight ADRs: a problem, the decision taken, the alternatives rejected, and a tracker of its own. Most of them are not about the language at all, and cover the tools and the presentation layer instead: how a bare name is resolved on disk, what the linter reports, how a tree of cards becomes a published site. They are working documents, kept for their motivation and their rejected alternatives, and where one disagrees with the specification the specification is right. The index is Proposals.

blocks.html_en: Vision¶

sentences.en: Vision¶

blocks.html_en: Markdown became the default plain text, and never got the part HTML had on its first day — links that mean something because they point into a knowledge graph, and a page that is part of a web rather than a file in a folder. Almost none of the ideas here are new; what is being attempted is a coherent specification of them.

content_html_zh:
超级 Markdown (.hmd) 是普通 Markdown 加上丰富的视觉效果以及知识图谱中的 Wiki 链接。 每个 .md 文件都已经是有效的 .hmd。

想看看它的实际效果吗？

HMD 教程一次性涵盖了整个语言 — 每个构造，其源代码显示在它所呈现的内容旁边。

TL;DR¶

  • CommonMark 的超集。 将 .md 文件重命名为 .hmd，它已经有效 - 没有任何破坏，并且一次采用一个文件的格式。
  • 名称，而不是路径。 [[tokens]] 在卡旁边查找，然后向上查找其父文件夹。 可能意味着两个文档的名称是一个错误而不是猜测。
  • 由文件组成的文件。 ![[glossary/token#^definition]] 将一个命名块拼接到另一页中。 编写一次定义并将其嵌入到任何需要的地方。
  • 内容丰富是假定的，不是可选的。 TeX 数学、D2 图表、标注、脚注、任务列表和表格是卡片可以携带的内容的一部分。 图表是文件中的文本和您可以阅读的差异，它会降级为自己标记的源而不是空白。
  • 规范就是工件。 Python CLI、MkDocs 插件和 VS Code 扩展都是围绕它的实现；他们遵守它而不是定义它。
  • 版本 0.x 是一个阶段，而不是范围。 解析器、linter、嵌入扩展器、渲染器和 MkDocs 插件现在可以使用。 对文档图和超出一棵树的命名空间的查询在大纲中指定并且未构建。

Language¶

三层堆叠在一个文件中。 在基础上，CommonMark 继承了整个内容 — 没有重新定义，也没有删除任何内容，这就是为什么 .md 文件已经是有效的卡。 在它之上是一个丰富的层——表格、脚注、任务列表、标注、TeX 数学、D2 图表——取自更广泛的 Markdown 生态系统，而不是在这里发明的，并且假设是存在的而不是可选的。 超层——可以说是最具创新性的部分，也是该格式存在的原因：一小组结构，它们都是一个想法的变体，命名另一个文档或一个文档的一部分。 上面两层是超级降价添加的内容，规范是修复它们的内容，而不是约定。

See [[tokens]] for the format, or pull one block in whole:

![[glossary/token#^definition]]

一张卡片可能会以 YAML frontmatter 打开，其中四个键对工具链意味着某种意义——标签、使用、导入、导航——而其他所有键都属于作者。 整个语言只需一页即可学会：HMD 教程。 该页面所教授的内容是 HMD 语言规范的规范说明。

Features¶

Wiki 链接到文档、标题和命名块；嵌入其中任何一个；具有显式导入的文件系统形模块； TeX 数学、D2 图表、标注、可折叠部分、脚注、表格和 GitHub 风格的 Markdown 基线。 HQL是一种基于文档图的查询语言，是保留的，尚未设计。

页面可以承载的内容是功能（功能），即功能（功能），而不是描述功能。 一个裸名称如何成为一个页面——主干行走、导入、错误的歧义以及模块/命名空间的区别——就是命名空间。

Tools¶

hmd lint 一棵树，将卡片渲染为 markdown 或 HTML，并转储解析后的图形。 缺少目标是一个警告，因为向前写是维基成长的方式；模棱两可或格式错误的错误是错误，因为这是格式拒绝猜测的一件事。

它们一共有三个，每个目录位于存储库中的 tools/ 下，每个目录都有自己的版本、README 和变更日志：

  • hmd — Python 系列，以超级降价形式发布到 PyPI：CLI（lint、渲染、图形）、其下的库以及构建此站点的 MkDocs 插件。 规范 - 当两种实现不一致时，这个定义了答案 - 并且它将托管语言服务器。
  • hmd-ts-core — @hyper-markdown/core，TypeScript 格式的第二种实现，而不是扩展代码，与规范工具的一致性语料库相同。
  • hmd-vsc-ext — VS Code 扩展，正在开发中：实时预览，使嵌入边界保持可见，以及反向链接、红色链接和诊断。

演示不是语言的一部分。 卡片是纯文本，因此编辑器、GitHub 或聊天窗口已经显示它。 MkDocs 插件将一棵卡片树构建到一个已发布的站点中 - 这是一本手工订购的书，里面有一个生成的 wiki - 并且扩展在输入时在编辑器中呈现一个。 它们之间的权衡是演示。

VS Code 扩展：左侧是卡片的源代码，右侧是渲染的卡片，在键入时更新。

Specification¶

规范性文本是一个文档，即 HMD 语言规范：卡是什么、每个构造的含义以及实现必须用它做什么。 它没有描述任何特定的程序，也没有程序的行为会覆盖它。

它是针对命名基线（CommonMark 0.31.2）进行陈述的，因为“markdown”命名的是一个系列而不是一个标准，并且未命名方言的超集没有指定任何内容。 它的版本与实现它的工具不同：hmd 的发布并不意味着新的语言版本，并且语言版本不会等待新的语言版本。 如果两个实现对于文本未确定的内容存在分歧，则由语言中立的一致性语料库决定。

语言为 0.1。 文本已起草，1.0之前会移动。

它如何到达那里是一个单独的过程，并且故意是一个正式的过程。 变更首先以编号技术提案（HMD-0001、HMD-0002 等）的形式提出，采用 RFC 和轻量级 ADR 的风格：问题、做出的决定、被拒绝的替代方案以及自己的跟踪器。 其中大多数根本不涉及语言，而是涵盖工具和表示层：如何在磁盘上解析裸名称、linter 报告什么、卡片树如何成为已发布的站点。 它们是工作文档，保留其动机和被拒绝的替代方案，如果有人不同意规范，则规范是正确的。 索引是提案。

Vision¶

Markdown 成为默认的纯文本，并且从未获得 HTML 第一天所拥有的部分 - 链接意味着某些东西，因为它们指向知识图，并且页面是网络的一部分而不是文件夹中的文件。 这里几乎没有一个想法是新的；正在尝试的是对它们进行连贯的规范。

更长的论点是，这不应该停留在一个存储库：独立创作和独立服务的超级降价，跨越差距命名，由人类、工具和人工智能从同一来源读取。 这个论点，以及其中有多少尚未建立，就是愿景。

Status¶

预发布。 扫描仪、解析器、linter、嵌入扩展器、渲染器和 MkDocs 插件均已实现和测试。 语言规范为 0.1，并且仍会变化。 活生生的例子是 wiki，它是从这个存储库中的 .hmd 卡生成的；每个功能的详尽清单、想法的来源以及被推迟或拒绝的功能列表。
